name: Plastic Bottle
description: Plastic bottles are usually made from PET plastic and can be recycled into new bottles, clothing, and carpets.
howToRecycle: Empty, rinse, squash to save space, and place in the plastic recycling bin.
creativeIdea: Turn it into a bird feeder, flower pot, or self-watering planter.
interestingFact: A recycled plastic bottle can be transformed into the fabric for a T-shirt!

name: Shampoo Bottle
description: Most shampoo bottles are made from HDPE plastic, one of the easiest plastics to recycle.
howToRecycle: Rinse thoroughly, remove the pump if possible, and recycle.
creativeIdea: Use it as a charging station or pen holder.
interestingFact: Recycled shampoo bottles are often turned into playground equipment.

name: Plastic Food Container
description: Clean food containers can be recycled into new plastic products.
howToRecycle: Wash away food residue before recycling.
creativeIdea: Store buttons, screws, or craft supplies.
interestingFact: One clean food container can be recycled into another useful household item.

name: Plastic Bucket
description: Plastic buckets are made from durable HDPE plastic and are recyclable.
howToRecycle: Clean and send to a recycling center or municipal collection.
creativeIdea: Convert it into a gardening planter or storage bin.
interestingFact: HDPE plastic is strong enough to be recycled into outdoor furniture.

name: Bottle Cap
description: Plastic bottle caps are made from PP or HDPE plastic.
howToRecycle: Keep the cap attached to the bottle if your local recycling program accepts it.
creativeIdea: Create colorful board games, magnets, or mosaics.
interestingFact: Thousands of bottle caps can become park benches after recycling.

name: Plastic Straw
description: Plastic straws are too small for most recycling machines.
howToRecycle: Reduce use by switching to reusable metal or bamboo straws.
creativeIdea: Use clean straws for children's craft projects.
interestingFact: One reusable straw can replace hundreds of disposable plastic straws every year.

name: Toothpaste Tube
description: Most toothpaste tubes contain multiple layers of plastic and aluminum.
howToRecycle: Recycle only through specialized collection programs.
creativeIdea: Cut open empty tubes to squeeze out every last bit of toothpaste before disposal.
interestingFact: Millions of toothpaste tubes end up in landfills every year because they are difficult to recycle.

name: Newspaper
description: Newspapers are one of the most commonly recycled paper products.
howToRecycle: Keep them dry and place them in the paper recycling bin.
creativeIdea: Use them as gift wrapping paper or for making paper bags.
interestingFact: Recycling one ton of newspaper saves about 17 mature trees.

name: Notebook
description: Paper notebooks can be recycled after removing plastic covers and spiral bindings.
howToRecycle: Separate non-paper parts before recycling.
creativeIdea: Use unused pages as a rough notebook.
interestingFact: Paper fibers can usually be recycled 5 to 7 times.

name: Cardboard Box
description: Clean cardboard is highly recyclable and is used to make new boxes.
howToRecycle: Flatten the box before placing it in the recycling bin.
creativeIdea: Build toy houses, organizers, or cat playhouses.
interestingFact: Many shipping boxes are already made from recycled cardboard.

name: Magazine
description: Glossy magazines are recyclable in most paper recycling programs.
howToRecycle: Recycle with other clean paper products.
creativeIdea: Create colorful collages and paper flowers.
interestingFact: Old magazines can become tissue paper after recycling.

name: Office Paper
description: Clean office paper is one of the easiest materials to recycle.
howToRecycle: Keep it free from food stains before recycling.
creativeIdea: Use one-sided sheets for notes or children's drawing.
interestingFact: Recycled office paper uses around 40% less energy than making new paper.

name: Greeting Card
description: Plain paper greeting cards are recyclable if they don't contain glitter or plastic decorations.
howToRecycle: Remove ribbons and plastic before recycling.
creativeIdea: Turn old greeting cards into bookmarks or gift tags.
interestingFact: Handmade greeting cards can often be recycled multiple times.

name: Book
description: Books can be donated, reused, or recycled when damaged.
howToRecycle: Donate readable books; recycle damaged ones after removing hard covers if required.
creativeIdea: Make a secret storage box or decorative shelf art.
interestingFact: Sharing a single book with many readers helps save paper and trees.

name: Glass Bottle
description: Glass bottles can be recycled endlessly without losing their quality or purity.
howToRecycle: Rinse the bottle, remove the cap if required, and place it in the glass recycling bin.
creativeIdea: Turn it into a flower vase, lamp, or decorative centerpiece.
interestingFact: A recycled glass bottle can return to a store shelf as a new bottle in about 30 days!

name: Glass Jar
description: Glass jars are commonly used for food storage and are completely recyclable.
howToRecycle: Wash the jar and remove metal lids before recycling.
creativeIdea: Use it to store spices, coins, or homemade candles.
interestingFact: Glass can be recycled forever without losing its strength.

name: Perfume Bottle
description: Most perfume bottles are made from recyclable glass.
howToRecycle: Empty completely and remove the spray pump if possible.
creativeIdea: Use as a mini flower vase or room decoration.
interestingFact: Beautiful perfume bottles are often collected as decorative art.

name: Glass Cup
description: Drinking glasses are made from a different type of glass than bottles.
howToRecycle: Donate if usable or dispose according to local waste rules.
creativeIdea: Use as a pen holder or candle holder.
interestingFact: Glass cups melt at different temperatures than bottles, so they usually cannot be recycled together.

name: Medicine Bottle
description: Glass medicine bottles can often be recycled after cleaning.
howToRecycle: Remove labels if possible and rinse thoroughly.
creativeIdea: Store beads, buttons, or small craft items.
interestingFact: Amber-colored medicine bottles protect medicines from harmful sunlight.

name: Window Glass
description: Window glass is treated differently and cannot usually be recycled with bottles.
howToRecycle: Take it to specialized construction recycling centers.
creativeIdea: Broken pieces can be used for mosaic artwork with proper safety.
interestingFact: Modern windows often contain coatings that improve energy efficiency.

name: Glass Bowl
description: Heat-resistant glass bowls are different from container glass.
howToRecycle: Donate if usable or dispose safely.
creativeIdea: Use cracked bowls as decorative plant holders.
interestingFact: Heat-resistant glass can survive temperatures that would crack ordinary bottles.

name: Aluminum Can
description: Aluminum cans are among the most valuable recyclable materials.
howToRecycle: Rinse, crush, and place them in the metal recycling bin.
creativeIdea: Create lanterns, pencil holders, or mini planters.
interestingFact: Recycling one aluminum can saves enough energy to power a TV for about 3 hours.

name: Steel Spoon
description: Steel spoons are durable and can be recycled repeatedly.
howToRecycle: Recycle with other scrap metals.
creativeIdea: Make decorative wind chimes or garden markers.
interestingFact: Steel is the world's most recycled material.

name: Cooking Pot
description: Old metal cooking pots contain valuable recyclable metals.
howToRecycle: Take them to a scrap metal collection center.
creativeIdea: Turn it into a flower pot or bird bath.
interestingFact: Many recycled cooking pots become parts of new kitchen utensils.

name: Tin Can
description: Food cans made from tin-coated steel are highly recyclable.
howToRecycle: Wash thoroughly before recycling.
creativeIdea: Create desk organizers or lanterns.
interestingFact: A recycled tin can may return to store shelves within two months.

name: Aluminum Foil
description: Clean aluminum foil can be recycled into new aluminum products.
howToRecycle: Remove food residue and roll small pieces into a ball.
creativeIdea: Use in art and science projects.
interestingFact: Recycling aluminum saves about 95% of the energy needed to produce new aluminum.

name: Copper Wire
description: Copper is one of the most valuable recyclable metals.
howToRecycle: Take to an authorized scrap metal dealer.
creativeIdea: Create handmade jewelry or sculptures.
interestingFact: Nearly 80% of all copper ever mined is still in use today because it can be recycled repeatedly.

name: Metal Bottle Cap
description: Metal bottle caps are small but completely recyclable.
howToRecycle: Collect several together before recycling.
creativeIdea: Make fridge magnets, keychains, or mosaic art.
interestingFact: Thousands of recycled bottle caps can be transformed into bicycle parts, appliances, and even cars.

name: Mobile Phone
description: Old mobile phones contain valuable metals such as gold, silver, and copper that can be recovered through recycling.
howToRecycle: Back up your data, remove the SIM card, and take the phone to an authorized e-waste recycling center.
creativeIdea: Reuse it as a music player, security camera, or digital alarm clock.
interestingFact: One million recycled mobile phones can recover about 24 kg of gold and over 250 kg of silver!

name: Laptop
description: Laptops contain recyclable metals, plastics, and electronic components.
howToRecycle: Erase personal data and hand it over to a certified e-waste collection center.
creativeIdea: Convert an old laptop into a home media server or learning computer.
interestingFact: More than 90% of a laptop's materials can be reused or recycled.

name: Laptop Charger
description: Chargers contain copper wires, plastic insulation, and electronic parts.
howToRecycle: Recycle through authorized e-waste collection points.
creativeIdea: Keep it as a spare charger if it still works.
interestingFact: Copper recovered from old chargers can be used to manufacture new electrical wires.

name: Computer Keyboard
description: Keyboards are made from plastic, rubber, and electronic circuits that can be recycled.
howToRecycle: Take it to an e-waste recycling facility.
creativeIdea: Use the keys for DIY keychains or decorative crafts.
interestingFact: A standard keyboard contains more than 100 reusable parts.

name: Computer Mouse
description: Computer mice contain plastic, copper, and small circuit boards.
howToRecycle: Dispose of it through an authorized e-waste recycler.
creativeIdea: Use the shell for STEM or robotics projects.
interestingFact: Even a small computer mouse contains recyclable metals that reduce the need for mining.

name: Earphones
description: Earphones contain copper wiring, magnets, and plastic components.
howToRecycle: Take them to an electronics recycling center.
creativeIdea: Reuse the magnets for science experiments.
interestingFact: Tiny earphones contain rare-earth magnets used in advanced electronics.

name: TV Remote
description: Remote controls contain plastic, circuit boards, and battery contacts.
howToRecycle: Remove the batteries and recycle the remote through an e-waste center.
creativeIdea: Reuse working remotes as spare controllers.
interestingFact: Removing batteries before recycling makes electronic recycling safer and more efficient.

name: Banana Peel
description: Banana peels naturally decompose and are excellent for composting.
howToRecycle: Place them in a compost bin instead of a recycling bin.
creativeIdea: Use composted banana peels as natural fertilizer for plants.
interestingFact: Banana peels are rich in potassium, which helps plants grow strong.

name: Orange Peel
description: Orange peels break down naturally and enrich compost.
howToRecycle: Add them to a compost pile.
creativeIdea: Dry the peels and use them as natural room fresheners.
interestingFact: Orange peels contain natural oils that can repel insects.

name: Eggshell
description: Eggshells are rich in calcium and improve compost quality.
howToRecycle: Crush and mix them into compost or garden soil.
creativeIdea: Use crushed eggshells around plants to help deter some garden pests.
interestingFact: Eggshells are about 95% calcium carbonate—the same mineral found in chalk.

name: Tea Leaves
description: Used tea leaves are biodegradable and make nutrient-rich compost.
howToRecycle: Compost the leaves after removing any plastic-containing tea bags.
creativeIdea: Mix used tea leaves into garden soil.
interestingFact: Tea leaves add nitrogen to compost, helping microorganisms thrive.

name: Coffee Grounds
description: Used coffee grounds improve soil structure and compost quality.
howToRecycle: Add them to a compost bin or garden soil in moderation.
creativeIdea: Use as a natural deodorizer for refrigerators.
interestingFact: Coffee grounds are loved by earthworms because they enrich compost.

name: Vegetable Peels
description: Vegetable peels decompose quickly and become nutrient-rich compost.
howToRecycle: Collect them separately and compost them.
creativeIdea: Use homemade compost to grow herbs and vegetables.
interestingFact: Nearly half of household kitchen waste can be composted instead of sent to landfills.

name: Coconut Shell
description: Coconut shells are biodegradable but decompose more slowly than fruit peels.
howToRecycle: Reuse them for crafts or add crushed pieces to compost.
creativeIdea: Make bird feeders, bowls, candle holders, or garden planters.
interestingFact: Coconut shells are so strong that they are also used to make charcoal, handicrafts, and eco-friendly products.

name: T-Shirt
description: Cotton and polyester T-shirts can often be reused or recycled into new fabric products.
howToRecycle: Donate wearable shirts or send damaged ones to a textile recycling center.
creativeIdea: Turn it into a reusable shopping bag or cleaning cloth.
interestingFact: Making one cotton T-shirt can require over 2,500 liters of water!

name: Jeans
description: Old jeans can be reused, donated, or recycled into insulation and new fabrics.
howToRecycle: Donate if wearable or recycle through textile collection programs.
creativeIdea: Make a backpack, pencil pouch, or cushion cover.
interestingFact: Some recycled denim is used to insulate houses and buildings.

name: Socks
description: Old socks can be reused for cleaning or recycled into textile fibers.
howToRecycle: Place them in textile recycling bins if available.
creativeIdea: Use them as dusting gloves or pet toys.
interestingFact: A lonely sock can still have a second life as a useful cleaning cloth.

name: Bath Towel
description: Old towels can be reused before being recycled.
howToRecycle: Donate clean towels to animal shelters or recycle them.
creativeIdea: Cut into reusable cleaning wipes.
interestingFact: Animal shelters often welcome donations of old towels and blankets.

name: Bedsheet
description: Bedsheets can be reused, donated, or recycled into textile fibers.
howToRecycle: Donate usable sheets or recycle worn-out ones.
creativeIdea: Sew into pillow covers or reusable bags.
interestingFact: Many recycled textiles are turned into carpet padding.

name: Curtain
description: Fabric curtains can often be reused or recycled.
howToRecycle: Donate clean curtains or send them to textile recycling facilities.
creativeIdea: Turn them into tablecloths or shopping bags.
interestingFact: Upcycling old curtains is a popular way to reduce textile waste.

name: School Bag
description: School bags made from fabric can often be repaired, donated, or recycled.
howToRecycle: Donate usable bags or recycle them through textile programs.
creativeIdea: Use as a storage organizer at home.
interestingFact: Donating one school bag can help another student continue their education.

name: Car Tire
description: Old tires can be recycled into playground surfaces, roads, and sports tracks.
howToRecycle: Take them to an authorized tire recycling center.
creativeIdea: Make a garden planter or playground swing.
interestingFact: Recycled rubber from tires is used in some athletic running tracks.

name: Rubber Slipper
description: Rubber slippers can be recycled through specialized recycling facilities.
howToRecycle: Donate usable slippers or recycle them where accepted.
creativeIdea: Use as a door stopper or plant pot base.
interestingFact: Millions of rubber slippers are discarded worldwide every year.

name: Rubber Band
description: Rubber bands are usually too small for standard recycling systems.
howToRecycle: Reuse them as many times as possible before disposal.
creativeIdea: Bundle cables or organize pens.
interestingFact: A single rubber band can often be reused hundreds of times.

name: Eraser
description: Most erasers are made from synthetic rubber mixed with other materials.
howToRecycle: Use completely before disposal.
creativeIdea: Small pieces can be used for stamp carving projects.
interestingFact: Modern erasers are usually made from synthetic rubber instead of natural rubber.

name: Rubber Gloves
description: Clean rubber gloves can sometimes be recycled through specialty programs.
howToRecycle: Wash thoroughly before taking them to a recycling facility.
creativeIdea: Reuse as gardening gloves if still in good condition.
interestingFact: Natural rubber comes from the sap of rubber trees.

name: Garden Hose
description: Garden hoses can be recycled through specialized rubber recycling centers.
howToRecycle: Take them to facilities that accept rubber products.
creativeIdea: Cut into pieces to protect tree trunks or tool handles.
interestingFact: Old garden hoses are often reused in farms before being recycled.

name: Rubber Ball
description: Rubber balls can sometimes be recycled depending on the material.
howToRecycle: Donate if usable or recycle through specialty programs.
creativeIdea: Use in pet games or children's activities.
interestingFact: Rubber's elasticity comes from long chains of natural or synthetic polymers.

name: Wooden Chair
description: Wooden chairs can often be repaired, reused, or recycled into wood products.
howToRecycle: Donate if usable or send to a wood recycling facility.
creativeIdea: Turn it into a plant stand or garden decoration.
interestingFact: A repaired wooden chair can last for decades, reducing the need to cut more trees.

name: Wooden Table
description: Solid wood tables are valuable because the wood can be reused many times.
howToRecycle: Repair, donate, or recycle through wood collection centers.
creativeIdea: Convert it into a workbench or bookshelf.
interestingFact: Reusing wooden furniture stores carbon that trees absorbed while growing.

name: Wooden Pencil
description: Wooden pencils are biodegradable and can be composted after removing non-wood parts.
howToRecycle: Separate the metal ferrule if possible before disposal.
creativeIdea: Use short pencils for craft decorations.
interestingFact: One tree can produce over 170,000 pencils!

name: Wooden Pallet
description: Wooden pallets are widely reused and recycled into furniture or mulch.
howToRecycle: Return reusable pallets or send damaged ones for recycling.
creativeIdea: Build coffee tables, benches, or garden planters.
interestingFact: Millions of pallets are repaired every year instead of being thrown away.

name: Ice Cream Stick
description: Wooden ice cream sticks are biodegradable and useful for crafts.
howToRecycle: Compost clean sticks or recycle where accepted.
creativeIdea: Make photo frames, bookmarks, or miniature bridges.
interestingFact: Popsicle-stick bridges are popular science fair projects around the world.

name: Wooden Door
description: Wooden doors can often be refurbished instead of discarded.
howToRecycle: Donate or recycle through construction waste facilities.
creativeIdea: Transform into a dining table or wall shelf.
interestingFact: Old wooden doors are commonly reused in vintage home décor.

name: Wooden Crate
description: Wooden crates are durable and easy to reuse.
howToRecycle: Repair or recycle into wood chips.
creativeIdea: Stack them into bookshelves or shoe racks.
interestingFact: Many fruit markets reuse the same wooden crates for years.

name: Battery
description: Batteries contain valuable metals but also hazardous chemicals that require special recycling.
howToRecycle: Take used batteries to authorized battery collection centers.
creativeIdea: Do not reuse damaged batteries. Instead, teach children about safe battery disposal.
interestingFact: A single improperly discarded battery can contaminate large amounts of soil and water.

name: LED Light Bulb
description: LED bulbs contain recyclable metals and electronic components.
howToRecycle: Recycle through an approved lighting or e-waste collection center.
creativeIdea: Use burnt-out bulbs as tiny decorative vases (only if safely prepared).
interestingFact: LED bulbs use up to 80% less electricity than traditional bulbs.

name: Ceramic Mug
description: Ceramic mugs cannot usually be recycled with glass because they melt at different temperatures.
howToRecycle: Donate if usable or dispose of safely.
creativeIdea: Use as a pen holder or small flower pot.
interestingFact: Ceramics are fired at temperatures above 1,000°C, making them extremely durable.

name: Mirror
description: Mirrors contain reflective coatings that prevent normal glass recycling.
howToRecycle: Take broken mirrors to construction waste facilities if available.
creativeIdea: Create decorative mosaic art using safely handled pieces.
interestingFact: The reflective layer behind a mirror is usually made from silver or aluminum.

name: Paint Can
description: Empty metal paint cans can often be recycled after the paint has completely dried.
howToRecycle: Allow leftover paint to dry before recycling the can.
creativeIdea: Use empty cans to store gardening tools or brushes.
interestingFact: Liquid paint should never be poured into drains because it can pollute waterways.

name: Disposable Face Mask
description: Most disposable masks contain mixed plastic fibers that are difficult to recycle.
howToRecycle: Cut the ear loops and dispose of them in general waste.
creativeIdea: Do not reuse disposable masks after use.
interestingFact: Improperly discarded masks can harm birds and marine animals if they become tangled in the straps.

name: Medicine Strip
description: Medicine blister packs are made from mixed plastic and aluminum layers, making them difficult to recycle.
howToRecycle: Dispose of them through pharmacy take-back or specialized recycling programs where available.
creativeIdea: Avoid crafts with used medicine packaging because it may contain medicine residue.
interestingFact: Many countries are developing new technologies to separate plastic and aluminum from medicine strips for recycling.
